doc: Band-pass layers G(s_{k-1}) - G(s_k) with G(s_-1) the image and G = _blur (scipy.ndimage.gaussian_filter(img, sigma, mode=("nearest", "wrap")): truncate 4.0 (radius int(4 sigma + 0.5), taps exp(-x^2 / (2 sigma^2)) normalized to sum 1, computed in float64), axis 0 (rows: "nearest" = clamp at the poles) THEN axis 1 (columns: "wrap" = periodic, folded as many times as the radius needs, also when it exceeds the width), each pass accumulating in float64 and rounding to the input dtype (so a float32 image is rounded to float32 between the two passes); sigma <= 1e-15 returns a copy, a radius that rounds to 0 (sigma < 0.125) is the identity.), and the low-pass residual G(s_last) (the image itself for no sigma); the layers and the residual sum back to the image (telescoping, up to float32 rounding). Layers are stacked in one array (shape (len(sigmas), h, w)). One sigma: one layer and the residual. Float32 chain (each blur rounds to float32 between its passes, a layer is a float32 difference): a float64-promoted result differs by <= 9e-8 in absolute value (a layer is a small difference, so its relative error is meaningless); the golden float32 tolerance.
